q: What is the minimum age to apply for a G1 licence in Ontario?
e: You must be at least 16, pass a vision test and pass the knowledge test.
s: To apply for a licence, you must be at least 16 years old

q: Without a driver-education course, how long must you hold your G1 before taking the G2 road test?
e: Level One lasts 12 months, or 8 months with an approved course.
s: Level One lasts 12 months.

q: If you pass an approved beginner driver education (BDE) course, how soon can you finish Level One (G1)?
e: An approved course cuts G1 from 12 months to 8.
s: If you pass an approved course, you can complete Level One in eight months.

q: How much driving experience must a G1 driver's accompanying driver have?
e: 4 years, with a full Class G (or higher) licence.
s: at least four years of driving experience

q: A G1 driver's accompanying driver must have a blood alcohol level of…
e: Under .05% (and zero if the accompanying driver is 21 or under).
s: a blood-alcohol level of less than .05% when accompanying you

q: How soon must you tell the Ministry of Transportation after changing your name or address?
e: 6 days. It's free.
s: You must tell the Ministry of Transportation within six days of changing your name or address.

q: How long do novice (G1/G2) drivers have to complete the graduated licensing process?
e: 5 years. If you don't finish (or requalify), you must start over at G1.
s: novice drivers have five years to complete the graduated-licensing process

q: Which of these is NOT a rule for G1 drivers?
a: You may drive alone between 5 a.m. and midnight
w: Your blood alcohol level must be zero
You may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.
Every person in the car must have a working seatbelt
e: A G1 driver must NEVER drive alone. An accompanying driver must sit in the front passenger seat.
s: You must not drive alone; an accompanying driver must sit in the front passenger seat.

q: A G1 driver may drive on a 400-series highway with a speed limit over 80 km/h ONLY when…
a: The accompanying driver is a driving instructor
w: It is daytime and traffic is light
The accompanying driver has 10 or more years of experience
The G1 driver has had their licence for 8 months
e: With a driving instructor, a G1 driver may drive on any road.
s: However, if your accompanying driver is a driving instructor, you may drive on any road.

q: When a G1 driver is driving, the accompanying driver must be the ONLY other person…
e: Others may sit in the back if each has a working seatbelt, but no one else in the front.
s: This is the only person who can be in the front seat with you while you drive.

q: Which of these is legal?
a: Carrying your licence every time you drive
w: Lending your licence to a learner in an emergency
Letting a friend use your licence as ID
e: You must carry your licence whenever you drive. Lending it, or having two, is illegal.
s: You must carry your licence with you whenever you drive.

q: A police officer asks for your licence, vehicle permit and insurance. When must you show them?
w: Only if you are being charged
e: There is no 24-hour grace period. That's a myth.
s: Contrary to popular belief, you do not have 24 hours to present these documents.

q: The G2 passenger limits for drivers 19 and under (midnight to 5 a.m.) do NOT apply when…
a: A fully licensed driver is in the front passenger seat, or the passengers are immediate family
w: The G2 driver has a clean record
The trip is shorter than 30 minutes
e: Those are the only two exemptions.
s: The passenger restrictions for G2 drivers aged 19 and under do not apply if you are accompanied by a fully–licensed driver in the front passenger seat, or if the passengers are members of your immediate family

q: Does time a driver spent with a valid G2 licence count toward the 4 years an accompanying driver needs?
a: Yes, as long as the G2 wasn't suspended
w: No, only full G time counts
Only if they took a driver-education course
Only half of the G2 time counts
e: Valid (not suspended) G2 time counts toward the 4 years.
s: Time spent at the Class G2 level, as long as the G2 licence was valid (not suspended), does count toward the accompanying driver’s four years of experience.

q: What should you bring to the G1 knowledge test?
a: Identification, money for the fees, and your glasses or contacts if you need them to drive
w: Your car, insurance and an accompanying driver
A doctor's note and two passport photos
e: ID, fees, and glasses or contacts if you wear them to drive. (You'll also take a vision test.)
s: Glasses or contact lenses (if you need to wear them to drive)

q: Your G2 licence is about to expire and you haven't finished graduated licensing. What can you do?
a: Requalify: pass a test and pay the 5-year licensing fee
w: Nothing; you automatically get a full G licence
Keep driving on it for 60 more days
e: If you don't finish or requalify before it expires, you must start again at G1.
s: you can regain or retain the same class of licence by passing a test and paying the five-year licensing fee

q: When are G1 drivers not allowed to drive?
e: No G1 driving from midnight to 5 a.m.
s: You must not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.

q: What blood alcohol level must a G2 driver have?
e: G1 and G2 drivers of any age must have zero blood alcohol.
s: You must not drive if you have been drinking alcohol. Your blood-alcohol level must be zero.

q: Without a driving instructor, which roads are off-limits to G1 drivers?
a: 400-series highways with limits over 80 km/h, and high-speed roads like the QEW, Don Valley Parkway and Gardiner Expressway
w: All roads with a speed limit over 50 km/h
Any road outside their home city
e: The E.C. Row Expressway and Conestoga Parkway are also off-limits.
s: You must not drive on 400-series highways with a posted speed limit over 80 km/h.

q: What must every person in a car driven by a G1 or G2 driver have?
e: The number of passengers is limited by the number of working seatbelts.
s: Each person in the vehicle must have a working seatbelt.

q: What kind of ID documents are accepted when you apply for a licence?
a: Original, valid documents showing your legal name and full date of birth
w: Expired documents less than a year old
e: Photocopies and expired documents are not accepted.
s: Documents must be original and valid. Photocopies and expired documents are not acceptable.

q: As of May 11, 2026, what must you declare when you apply for a Class G licence?
a: That Ontario is your primary place of residence and that your presence in Canada is legal
w: That you have taken a driving course
e: This declaration was added on May 11, 2026.
s: As of May 11, 2026, when you apply for your class G or class M licence, you will need to declare that

q: Who must doctors and optometrists report to the Ministry of Transportation?
a: Anyone over 16 who has a condition that may make it unsafe for them to drive
w: Only people who ask to be reported
e: Doctors and optometrists must report it by law. Your licence may be suspended until the condition is shown to be safe.
s: By law, doctors and optometrists must report the name and address of anyone over 16 who has a condition that may make it unsafe for him or her to drive.

q: A G1 driver's accompanying driver may have demerit points on their licence. What can't their licence be?
w: From another class, like Class A
e: Demerit points are OK. A suspended licence is not.
s: The accompanying driver’s licence may have demerit points, but it cannot be suspended.

q: When may you lend your driver’s licence?
w: To a person learning to drive.
e: Official MTO sample question. Lending your licence is always illegal.
s: Lend your licence
